E1.evidence: Reproduction steps (rqt with use_sim_time, tf tree view, restart `ros2 bag play --clock`) and a full traceback ending in "TypeError: Buffer.time_jump_callback() takes 1 positional argument but 2 were given"; maintainer sloretz diagnoses it and clalancette/ahcorde merge the fix. https://github.com/ros2/geometry2/issues/710

E2.interface_kind: library API (jump-callback registration and invocation signature)
E2.evidence: tf2_ros_py's Buffer registers `self.jump_handle = self.clock.create_jump_callback(threshold, post_callback=self.time_jump_callback)`; rclpy invokes the post callback as `original_callback(TimeJump(clock_change, duration))`, per its declared contract ":param post_callback: Callback to be called after new time is set. The callback" / "must accept a single argument that is a ``TimeJump``." (rclpy 7.1.2 clock.py). tf2_ros_py's method was declared `def time_jump_callback(time_jump: TimeJump):`, so the bound method accepts no argument. The failure is the arity of a callable crossing the library boundary (sloretz: "`Buffer.time_jump_callback()` takes 1 positional argument (a Buffer instance) but 2 were given (a Buffer instance and a `TimeJump` instance)."); the resolving edit is inside tf2_ros_py. Not deployment wiring or build.

E3.evidence: PAIR: rclpy's clock (driven by /clock under use_sim_time) calls tf2_ros_py's registered post callback with a TimeJump when a backward jump occurs (bag replay restarted).

E4.evidence: Observed crash: "TypeError: Buffer.time_jump_callback() takes 1 positional argument but 2 were given" followed by "[1]    295333 IOT instruction (core dumped)  rqt --ros-args -p use_sim_time:=True" https://github.com/ros2/geometry2/issues/710

units.name: rclpy

units.name: tf2_ros_py
units.revision_basis: Broken: jazzy debian packages on 2024-09-23; the latest geometry2 jazzy release tag before that date is 0.36.4 (da10f77d98ab97d2dfdfa9bfc4c98042a8ad7c3d, 2024-05-29), which is also the revision of buffer.py that sloretz links ("https://github.com/ros2/geometry2/blob/da10f77d98ab97d2dfdfa9bfc4c98042a8ad7c3d/tf2_ros_py/tf2_ros/buffer.py#L107-L109"). Exact binary version inferred. Resolved: jazzy backport commit 646342c6164e837d69460e3d28e7a025396544f6 (PR #712), whose single parent is 0.36.4 and whose only change is the one-line signature fix; the reporter tested the identical diff from PR #711 (rolling merge efc784597ccbd8d246794e72b20358deab4ab114, head 5b337f94b10b08e1e78d618c70a16b552f2d93e0) on jazzy.

failed_conditions.quote: The type annotation `def time_jump_callback(time_jump: TimeJump):` is incorrect. The first argument of a method is always bound to an instance of the class, and by convention this argument is usually called `self`. If I fix the argument name and the type annotation then the reason for the error becomes clear: `def time_jump_callback(self: "Buffer"):`. `Buffer.time_jump_callback()` takes 1 positional argument (a Buffer instance) but 2 were given (a Buffer instance and a `TimeJump` instance).

loudness_evidence: No build/import/activation diagnostic: the mismatched callable is accepted at registration and the error surfaces only when rclpy invokes it on a time jump, as a run-time Python exception that crashes rqt: "TypeError: Buffer.time_jump_callback() takes 1 positional argument but 2 were given". The reporter notes: "interestingly python only crashes once the method is actually called, not when it is referenced as `buffer.time_jump_callback`" and that a static checker (pyright) would flag it, but none ran. https://github.com/ros2/geometry2/issues/710

resolution.summary: tf2_ros_py: declare the jump callback as a method taking the TimeJump argument, `def time_jump_callback(self, time_jump: TimeJump):` (rolling efc784597ccbd8d246794e72b20358deab4ab114, jazzy 646342c6164e837d69460e3d28e7a025396544f6). rclpy unchanged.
resolution.evidence: Reporter after applying PR #711 on jazzy: "this fixes the problem all the way to rqt-tf-tree in jazzy! now i get" / "[WARN] [1727982819.603705139] [tf2_buffer]: Detected jump back in time. Clearing tf buffer." / "when without the fix rqt would crash, as expected." https://github.com/ros2/geometry2/pull/711 . Resolved composition: rclpy 7.1.2 with tf2_ros_py at 0.36.4 plus the one-line fix, which is exactly commit 646342c6164e837d69460e3d28e7a025396544f6.

notes: Class `other`: the mismatch is the arity of a callback passed across a library API (rclpy declares `post_callback: Optional[Callable[[TimeJump], None]]`; tf2_ros_py passes a bound method that takes no argument); none of the ROS-interface classes names a callable-signature mismatch, and no element was renamed or retyped between revisions. The body `self.clear()` would also have failed (no `self` in scope) had the arity matched. The crash appeared in the rqt tf tree plugin (rqt_tf_tree), which only hosts the tf2_ros Buffer; the failing call is rclpy -> tf2_ros_py, as the traceback shows ("File \"/opt/ros/jazzy/lib/python3.12/site-packages/rclpy/clock.py\", line 242, in callback_shim"). The issue was first filed against rclpy and moved to geometry2 by clalancette after sloretz's diagnosis ("This is a bug in `tf2_ros_py`."). Loudness recorded as silent_documented because the only diagnostic is a run-time exception at invocation, not a build/connect/activate diagnostic.
